item.title: Event Horizon Telescope views the dynamics and geometry of a black hole jet in extreme detail
item.description: The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT), a massive international collaboration of scientists and radio observatories, is like the gift that keeps on giving. In 2019, the EHT Collaboration gave us the first image of a black hole: the supermassive black hole (SMBH) at the heart of the M87 galaxy (M87*). In 2022, it provided the first image of Sagittarius A*, the SMBH at the center of the Milky Way. Between 2024 and 2026, the international array also produced detailed images of the relativistic jets emanating from 3C 84 and M87*. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI simulates electron hops over far longer times than conventional quantum calculations
item.description: To predict how a material will behave, we need to know which atoms are located where. This allows us, for example, to explain whether a material is suitable as a catalyst for certain chemical reactions. But often, that is not enough: even if all the atoms stay exactly where they are, the distribution of electric charge within the material can change dramatically. Electrons can jump from one atom to another, changing the forces between atoms as well as the material's chemical reactivity. Fuente: Phys.org.
